newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up on bargain hunting.

text.p: Thai stocks rallied to close higher for the third consecutive day on Wednesday, gaining 1.78 percent on local bargain hunting and window dressing of year-end corporate balance sheets, brokers said.
The SET index rose 14.70 points to 841.42 on thin 2.07 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index gained 1.14 points to 62.83.
"The index rose purely on local speculation and buying by some listed firms seeking to window dress year-end balance sheets," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.

Brokers attributed the thin turnover to closure of several regional markets to celebrate Christmas. Traders said the festive season prompted some of them to shut offices before the market closed on Wednesday.
All key sectors registered gains on Wednesday.

Bangkok Bank topped the active list, rising two baht to 195, Dhana Siam gained 3.50 to 66.50, Siam Cement added 12 to 792, Advanced Info rose 4 to 242, Banpu rallied six to 474, and Lanna Lignite advanced six to 230.
Brokers saw support at 830 and resistance at 855 on Thursday. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
